title: Noncommuting entropy production and thermal secular models

items.title: Finite energy-resolved GKSL thermal model
items.statement: Let $d\geq1$ and let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$ with its standard complex inner product. Let $H=H^*$ on $\mathcal H$ be a Hamiltonian matrix with entries in joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ be a finite family of dimensionless Hermitian matrices, where $m\geq0$. Write the finite spectral decomposition $H=\sum_{E\in\operatorname{spec}(H)} E P_E$, where $P_E$ are pairwise orthogonal spectral projections and $\sum_E P_E=I_d$. The Bohr-frequency set is $$\Omega_H:=\{(E'-E)/\hbar:E,E'\in\operatorname{spec}(H)\}\subset\mathbb R,$$ whose frequencies have units seconds$^{-1}$. For each $\omega\in\Omega_H$ and $1\leq a\leq m$, define the dimensionless energy-resolved coupling $$S_a(\omega):=\sum_{\substack{E,E'\in\operatorname{spec}(H)\\E'-E=\hbar\omega}}P_E S_a P_{E'}.$$ Let $\beta\in\mathbb R$ have units joules$^{-1}$. For each $\omega\in\Omega_H$, choose a finite positive-semidefinite rate matrix $\Gamma(\omega)=(\gamma_{ab}(\omega))_{a,b=1}^m$, with entries in seconds$^{-1}$, and require the thermal balance relation $$\gamma_{ab}(-\omega)=e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}\gamma_{ba}(\omega).$$ Let $H_{\rm LS}=H_{\rm LS}^*$ be a Hermitian matrix with units joules satisfying $[H_{\rm LS},H]=0$. For dimensionless $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, the finite energy-resolved generator is the linear map $$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H+H_{\rm LS},X]+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_H}\sum_{a,b=1}^{m}\gamma_{ab}(\omega)\left(S_b(\omega)X S_a(\omega)^*-\frac12\{S_a(\omega)^*S_b(\omega),X\}\right),$$ where $[A,B]=AB-BA$, $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$, and $A^*$ is the conjugate transpose. The finite sums define a linear map with units seconds$^{-1}$. This is an adopted finite effective model specification; the definition asserts no microscopic weak-coupling convergence or physical applicability.

items.title: Thermal balance makes Gibbs stationary
items.statement: Let $d\geq1$, let $H=H^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have entries in joules and a finite spectral decomposition $H=\sum_E E P_E$ with pairwise orthogonal projections summing to $I_d$, and let $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ be a finite family of dimensionless Hermitian matrices, where $m\geq0$. Set $\Omega_H=\{(E'-E)/\hbar:E,E'\in\operatorname{spec}(H)\}$ and, for each $\omega\in\Omega_H$, define $S_a(\omega)=\sum_{E'-E=\hbar\omega}P_E S_aP_{E'}$. Suppose that the positive-semidefinite rate matrices $\Gamma(\omega)=(\gamma_{ab}(\omega))$, $\omega\in\Omega_H$, have entries in seconds$^{-1}$ and satisfy $\gamma_{ab}(-\omega)=e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}\gamma_{ba}(\omega)$, with $\beta\in\mathbb R$ in joules$^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Let $H_{\rm LS}=H_{\rm LS}^*$ have entries in joules and commute with $H$, and let $\mathcal L$ be the finite generator $$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H+H_{\rm LS},X]+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_H}\sum_{a,b=1}^{m}\gamma_{ab}(\omega)\left(S_b(\omega)X S_a(\omega)^*-\frac12\{S_a(\omega)^*S_b(\omega),X\}\right).$$ For $Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})>0$, define the faithful Gibbs density $\sigma_\beta:=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$. For time $t\geq0$ measured in seconds, $T_t:=e^{t\mathcal L}$ is completely positive and trace-preserving, and $T_t(\sigma_\beta)=\sigma_\beta$. This statement asserts stationarity only; it asserts neither uniqueness of the stationary density nor convergence to $\sigma_\beta$.

items.title: Stationary finite quantum semigroups decrease relative entropy
items.statement: Let $d\geq1$ and let $\mathcal L:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be complex-linear. Define $T_t:=e^{t\mathcal L}:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^n\mathcal L^n/n!$ for $t\geq0$, and assume that each $T_t$ is completely positive and trace-preserving; the exponential gives $T_{t+s}=T_t\circ T_s$. Let $\sigma=\sigma^*>0$ satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$ and $T_t(\sigma)=\sigma$ for every $t\geq0$. For a density matrix $\rho$, define the finite quantum relative entropy $$D(\rho\|\sigma):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\sigma),$$ using the natural logarithm, the finite spectral logarithm on the support of $\rho$, and $0\log0:=0$. Since $\sigma$ is positive definite, $D(\rho\|\sigma)$ is finite for every density $\rho$. Then $t\mapsto D(T_t\rho\|\sigma)$ is nonincreasing on $[0,\infty)$. If $t$ is interpreted as seconds, $\mathcal L$ has units seconds$^{-1}$; the statement is mathematical and asserts no physical applicability. At every $t\geq0$ for which $\rho_t:=T_t\rho$ is positive definite, its derivative exists (as a right derivative at $t=0$) and $$\frac{d}{dt}D(\rho_t\|\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\mathcal L(\rho_t)(\log\rho_t-\log\sigma)\right)\leq0.$$ At singular $\rho_t$ this logarithmic derivative is not asserted; the extended-real upper right Dini derivative is at most zero. No detailed-balance assumption, strict decay, unique stationary state, or convergence to $\sigma$ is asserted.

title: Noncommuting entropy production and thermal secular models — Examples

items.title: Dephasing fixes many states
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional completely positive trace-preserving semigroup, nonincrease of relative entropy to a faithful stationary Gibbs density is sufficient to guarantee that the Gibbs density is the unique stationary density and that every initial density converges to it.
